```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sato_2025_midazolam_rat"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sato_2025_midazolam_rat"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-03949-x> (open access)

Sato et al. gave a single 400 ug/kg intravenous bolus of midazolam to
anaesthetised, mechanically ventilated male Sprague-Dawley rats, three of
which were then placed on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) 2 min
after the dose while three sham-operated rats served as controls. Plasma
midazolam was measured for 180 min and fitted with a two-compartment
population PK model in NONMEM. ECMO was the only covariate tested; it was
retained as a 3.02-fold multiplier on the central volume. The paper also
reports lower hepatic CYP3A (testosterone 6-beta-hydroxylation) activity in
ECMO-treated livers; that in-vitro measurement is not part of the PK model.

# Population

Twelve male Sprague-Dawley rats (14-16 weeks old, 400-450 g) were used; six
of them formed the midazolam PK study, three on ECMO and three sham-operated
(Methods, Experimental design). ECMO drained the right internal jugular vein
and returned blood through the left common carotid artery cannula at an
auxiliary flow of 60-70 mL/kg/min; the circuit was primed with 7 mL saline
and 1 mL heparin (Supplementary Information 2). Forty-eight plasma samples
were collected at eight times: 2 min after the dose (before ECMO started)
and 5-180 min after ECMO initiation (Results, PK analysis).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Sato_2025_midazolam_rat")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL) | log(0.69 L/h) | Table 3, theta CL (RSE 18.0%) |
| `lvc` (V1, sham) | log(0.22 L) | Table 3, theta V1 (RSE 41.2%) |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(0.49 L) | Table 3, theta V2 (RSE 34.4%) |
| `lq` (Q) | log(0.29 L/h) | Table 3, theta Q (RSE 20.5%) |
| `e_ecmo_status_vc` | 3.02 | Table 3, dic (ECMO) (RSE 41.7%); assigned to V1 by the Results text and the Discussion ('an increase in V1 (0.66 vs. 0.22 L)') |
| `etalcl` | 0.617 = log(0.924^2 + 1) | Table 3, omega CL = 92.4 CV% |
| `etalvc` | 0.216 = log(0.491^2 + 1) | Table 3, omega V1 = 49.1 CV% |
| `propSd` | 0.395 | Table 3, proportional residual = 39.5% |
| IIV model `theta_i = theta * exp(eta_i)` | n/a | Methods, PK analysis, first equation |
| Covariate model `theta_i = theta_pop * dic^ECMO * exp(eta_i)` | n/a | Methods, PK analysis, third equation (see Assumptions) |
| Residual model `Y_obs = Y_pred * (1 + eps_prop)` | n/a | Methods, PK analysis, second equation; Results ('two-compartment model with a proportional error') |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Two-compartment model with V1, V2, CL, Q (Methods, PK analysis) |

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. Two virtual arms of 200 rats each (ECMO and
sham) receive 400 ug/kg as an intravenous bolus. Body weight is drawn
uniformly from the 400-450 g range of the paper and is used only to compute
the dose in ug: the model's volumes and clearances are absolute values for
rats of that size, not per-kilogram parameters.

```{r cohort}
# One record per rat per sampling time. The observation grid runs to 3 h,
# the end of the paper's sampling, so that PKNCA sees the same window as the
# paper's NCA.
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 3, by = 1 / 12), c(2, 5, 15, 30, 45) / 60)))

make_arm <- function(n, ecmo, dose_ugkg, id_offset = 0L) {
  rats <- tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT = runif(n, 0.400, 0.450),
    ECMO_STATUS = ecmo,
    group = if (ecmo == 1) "ECMO" else "Sham",
    amt = dose_ugkg * WT
  )
  doses <- rats |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(rats |> select(-amt), time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

set.seed(19363)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(19363)
events <- bind_rows(
  make_arm(200, ecmo = 1, dose_ugkg = 400, id_offset = 0L),
  make_arm(200, ecmo = 0, dose_ugkg = 400, id_offset = 200L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Sato_2025_midazolam_rat")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("group", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3 and Figure 5: observed profiles against the model

The paper's Figure 3 shows the mean +/- SD of the three rats per group and
Figure 5 a 500-replicate VPC. The open circles below are the group means
read off Figure 3 by the maintainers (approximate, to the resolution of the
printed axis); the bands are the 5th-95th and 25th-75th percentiles of 200
simulated rats per group with the median as a line.

```{r figure-3-5, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
fig3_means <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~time_min, ~Cc,
  "ECMO",   2, 395,
  "ECMO",   5, 243,
  "ECMO",  15, 185,
  "ECMO",  30, 142,
  "ECMO",  45,  90,
  "ECMO",  60,  97,
  "ECMO", 120,  78,
  "ECMO", 180,  62,
  "Sham",   2, 655,
  "Sham",   5, 390,
  "Sham",  15, 205,
  "Sham",  30, 132,
  "Sham",  45,  85,
  "Sham",  60,  60,
  "Sham", 120,  28,
  "Sham", 180,  15
) |>
  mutate(time = time_min / 60)

vpc <- sim |>
  group_by(group, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q25 = quantile(Cc, 0.25),
    Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50), Q75 = quantile(Cc, 0.75),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q25, ymax = Q75), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig3_means, aes(time, Cc), shape = 1, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after midazolam (h)", y = "Midazolam (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figures 3 and 5 of Sato 2025 (400 ug/kg IV bolus)."
  )
```

Up to about 45 min the observed means of both groups lie near the simulated
median (at 15 min, for example, 205 vs about 220 ng/mL in the sham group and
185 vs about 155 ng/mL with ECMO). The late ECMO means (2-3 h) sit near
the simulated 95th percentile: the final model carries no ECMO
effect on clearance, so it does not reproduce the slower terminal decline the
authors saw in the ECMO arm by noncompartmental analysis (Table 2).

## Figure 6: typical-value profiles at 200, 400 and 800 ug/kg

Figure 6 shows model-predicted profiles for three doses with and without
ECMO over 0-12 h and 0-3 h. The typical-value curves below are for a 425 g
rat (the middle of the 400-450 g range).

```{r figure-6, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
grid6 <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.05), seq(0, 0.5, by = 0.01))))
ev6 <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  dose_ugkg = c(200, 400, 800),
  ECMO_STATUS = c(0, 1)
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), amt = dose_ugkg * 0.425)
ev6 <- bind_rows(
  ev6 |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(ev6 |> select(-amt), time = grid6) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim6 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev6,
  keep = c("dose_ugkg"), rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    group = ifelse(ECMO_STATUS == 1, "ECMO", "Sham"),
    dose = factor(paste(dose_ugkg, "ug/kg"), levels = paste(c(200, 400, 800), "ug/kg"))
  )

ggplot(sim6, aes(time, Cc, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  scale_colour_grey(start = 0.7, end = 0) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Midazolam (ng/mL)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6 (a, b) of Sato 2025; typical rat of 425 g."
  )
```

```{r figure-6-check}
# Structural checks on the typical-value solve: initial concentration is
# dose / V1, the ECMO arm's is exactly 1/3.02 of the sham arm's, and the
# AUC to infinity equals dose / CL. These use the same parameters on both
# sides, so the tolerance is numerical only.
c0 <- sim6 |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  select(dose_ugkg, group, Cc) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = Cc)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(c0$Sham / (c0$dose_ugkg * 0.425 / 0.22) - 1)) < 1e-6,
  max(abs(c0$ECMO / c0$Sham - 1 / 3.02)) < 1e-6
)
auc12 <- sim6 |>
  group_by(dose_ugkg, group) |>
  summarise(auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2), .groups = "drop")
# Trapezoidal AUC0-12h against dose/CL: the 1.7-h terminal half-life leaves
# ~1% of the AUC beyond 12 h and the 0.05-h grid adds ~1% trapezoid error.
stopifnot(max(abs(auc12$auc / (auc12$dose_ugkg * 0.425 / 0.69) - 1)) < 0.05)
knitr::kable(c0, digits = 0, caption = "Typical-value concentration at time 0 (ng/mL).")
```

At 400 ug/kg the sham typical-value curve starts at about 773 ng/mL,
matching the ~780 ng/mL read off Figure 6, and 800 ug/kg doubles it. The
ECMO curves start 3.02-fold lower. The Figure 6 caption does not say which
panel is which group; panel (b) starts lower, and the Results state that
ECMO concentrations were lower immediately after the dose, so (b) is read as
ECMO. Its initial concentrations are only about half of the sham ones (~390
vs ~780 ng/mL at 400 ug/kg), which does not follow from a 3.02-fold V1
effect; see Assumptions and deviations.

# PKNCA validation

Table 2 of the paper reports a noncompartmental analysis of the observed
data over 0-180 min. The same analysis is run here on the simulated rats,
grouped by ECMO status.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)
# The time-zero observation exists in every subject (the grid starts at 0);
# for an IV bolus it holds the post-dose concentration, which is correct.
stopifnot(all(tapply(sim_nca$time, sim_nca$id, min) == 0))

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id, route = "intravascular")
# AUC over the sampled 0-3 h window; half-life, CL and Vss from the same
# 0-3 h data extrapolated to infinity, as the paper's moment analysis does.
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = c(3, Inf),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  cl.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  vss.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Table 2 labels AUC0-180 min in ng/mL-hr, but its values (17,004 and 14,994)
are 60 times what the Figure 3 means integrate to in ng*h/mL (about 250 for
the sham group); the column is in ng*min/mL. The reference AUCs below are
the Table 2 values divided by 60. CL and Vss are in L and L/h because the
dose is in ug and concentrations in ng/mL (ug/L).

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~auclast, ~half.life, ~cl.obs, ~vss.obs,
  "ECMO", 17004.0 / 60, 7.4, 0.69, 1.21,
  "Sham", 14994.1 / 60, 0.88, 1.05, 0.92
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "group",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", half.life = "h", cl.obs = "L/h", vss.obs = "L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (median) vs. published (mean, Table 2) NCA over 0-3 h. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

The PKNCA helper labels clearance and Vss as CL/F and Vss/F; the dose is
intravenous, so F = 1. Starred rows follow from the model structure and are
not transcription errors:

* **Clearance.** The final model has one clearance (0.69 L/h) for both
  groups; ECMO was retained on V1 only. The simulated median clearance
  (about 0.7 L/h in both arms) matches the ECMO rats' NCA clearance (0.69
  L/h) and is below the sham rats' (1.05 L/h), so the simulated ECMO AUC is
  also below the Table 2 value.
* **Half-life.** The paper's ECMO half-life is 7.4 +/- 15.3 h over three
  rats, a spread that requires one rat with a half-life of more than a day;
  the sham value is 0.88 h. The model's terminal half-life is 1.7 h in both
  groups, and a 0-3 h fit to the simulated rats gives about 1.6 h, between
  the two.
* **Vss.** The model's typical Vss is V1 + V2 = 0.71 L (sham) and 1.15 L
  (ECMO), against 0.92 and 1.21 L by NCA.

```{r nca-gate}
# Structural gate: the sham-arm AUC0-3h is set by dose and CL and moves by
# tens of percent with a wrong dose basis (per kg vs absolute), unit or CL.
# Model typical value 220 ng*h/mL vs 250 from Table 2; the median over 200
# simulated rats is within about 15% of the typical value at any seed.
auc_sham <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(group == "Sham", PPTESTCD == "auclast")
stopifnot(abs(median(auc_sham$PPORRES) / (14994.1 / 60) - 1) < 0.35)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate equation.** The paper prints the ECMO model as
  `theta_i = theta_pop * dic * exp(eta_i)` with `dic` the 0/1 ECMO
  indicator, which would set the parameter to zero in the sham rats. The
  model uses the conventional reading `theta_pop * 3.02^ECMO_STATUS`, which
  reproduces the Discussion's statement that V1 is 0.66 L with ECMO and 0.22
  L without.
* **Parameter carrying the ECMO effect.** One Results sentence reads "ECMO
  significantly influenced the CL of MDZ, and V1 was 3.02 times higher in
  the presence of ECMO". Table 3 has a single ECMO coefficient, the
  Discussion assigns it to V1 (0.66 vs 0.22 L), and the reported typical CL
  has no ECMO-specific value, so the effect is placed on V1 only.
* **IIV scale.** Table 3 reports IIV as CV%. The paper does not say how CV%
  was computed from the NONMEM variance; the conventional log-normal
  relation `omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)` was used (0.617 for CL, 0.216 for V1).
  Read as `omega = CV`, the variances would be 0.854 and 0.241.
* **Timing of ECMO.** Midazolam was given 2 min before ECMO started, and the
  first sample was taken before ECMO began. The paper's covariate is
  per-rat, so the model applies the ECMO volume from the dose onward, as the
  paper did.
* **Dose basis.** The model's parameters are absolute (L, L/h). The dose in
  the simulations is 400 ug/kg times a body weight drawn from 400-450 g,
  which reproduces the ~780 ng/mL initial concentration of the sham
  typical-value curve in Figure 6.
* **Figure 6, ECMO panel.** The published ECMO curves start at about half
  the sham concentration, not at 1/3.02 of it. The model is encoded from
  Table 3 and not adjusted to match the figure; the figure may show the
  mean of the Monte Carlo replicates, whose spread is not stated.
* **Figure 3 means** were read from the printed figure by the maintainers
  for the overlay only; no model value depends on them.
* No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (EuropePMC
  search, 2026-11-04).
